reconverted_2026_11_07.previous_converter: act_convert.py, the 2026-11-06 converter (kept outside the repository)
reconverted_2026_11_07.why: act_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character with a code of F000 or more, which is how the register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept Symbol-font characters typed as text as raw private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. act_convert_sym.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0D7 ·, F0B4 ×, F02D −, F0B7 •, F0A3 ≤, F0B3 ≥ and the like) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: Only bullets. 51 Symbol-font bullets kept as U+F0B7 (empty boxes) are written as "•": the s 49(1) list of relevant provisions of the Magistrates Court Act 1930 (lines 552-555: ss 314-317), the dictionary's note 2 list of terms defined by the Legislation Act (lines 1168-1211) and the examples under the definition of post-mortem examination (lines 1249-1251). Nothing had been dropped: no <w:sym> character is in the Word file, and no decimal point, multiplication sign, minus sign, inequality or tick box was lost. Reconverted from the same Word file (same sha256); the notice header is kept exactly and a diff against the first deposit shows no other change (same lines, same character and byte counts).
reconverted_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: baseline-2026-11 relies on no changed line for anything the bullet glyph affects (its s 49(2)(c) rule rests on the words naming Magistrates Court Act 1930 s 315, unchanged; it does not use the dictionary's note 2 list or the post-mortem examination examples)
